Case_22006/figure1.png.source_caption: Fig 1. Faint erythematous macular rash on face, arms and legs, trunk, and palms of hands

description.short_caption: Faint erythematous macular rash on face, arms, trunk, and palms.
description.detailed_description: This composite image shows faint erythematous macular lesions distributed across multiple anatomical sites including the forehead, axilla, upper arm, and palm. The rash appears diffuse and non-confluent, with individual macules visible against the skin. The lesions are subtle and do not exhibit scaling or pustulation. The image highlights the rash's presence on both exposed and less exposed areas of the body.
visible_findings: diffuse distribution across face, arms, trunk, and palms

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral basilar infiltrates.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph demonstrating bilateral opacities predominantly in the lower lung zones. The infiltrates appear diffuse and hazy, consistent with a pattern of consolidation or interstitial involvement. The heart and mediastinal structures are partially obscured by the overlying opacities. No clear evidence of pleural effusion or pneumothorax is visible.
visible_findings: hazy opacities in lower lung zones

Case_22006/figure3.png.source_caption: Fig 3. Bilateral airspace opacities of posterior lungs and moderate pulmonary edema

description.short_caption: CT chest showing bilateral airspace opacities and pulmonary edema.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral airspace opacities predominantly in the posterior lung fields. There is evidence of moderate pulmonary edema, with increased interstitial markings and ground-glass opacities. The heart appears enlarged, suggesting possible cardiomegaly. The findings are consistent with fluid overload or an infectious/inflammatory process.
